There is potential but… BEWARE THE A.I.. I want to start off by saying that this app has potential. There are legitimate advisors on here who are very human, can indeed connect with you on an energetic level and provide you valuable insight with details regarding your situation with honesty and empathy. However, this platform has a HUGE problem with advisors using AI/ChatGPT. 

The people over at PsychicBook clearly do not go through an extensive qualification process. If you are familiar with ChatGPT at all, like me - you will be able to tell IMMEDIATELY. Try having a profound conversation with ChatGPT and you will see for yourself, then go back and compare readings you have had with some of these advisors, you will be in shock. It’s honestly pretty sad. I understand this is a business, they want to hook people to have more and more sessions with them. I get it. I even understand the clearly AI generated advisor photos, they probably want to conceal their identities. That’s fine - but these people are shamelessly using ChatGPT. 

Here are some ways you can tell: They are overly optimistic and never disagree. They send entire paragraphs at RAPID SPEED, I’m talking, 2 entire 4-5 sentence paragraphs in 1-2 minutes, and okay let’s say they are EXTREMELY fast typers and pick up an insane amount of information about you very quickly (unlikely), the paragraph structures themselves are 100% ChatGPT style. The excessive use of hyphens, the dramatic way of concluding statements. You may often see them say something like “This is not just a ___, it is a ___.” If that makes any sense. I went as far and sharing some responses with ChatGPT and it was in complete agreement that the responses were generated by it, explaining all the reasons why. 

I just hope this review is able to at least help someone, and save them from wasting their money on the wrong advisor. At least the app offers free consultations, so it often helps in weeding out the AI. Like I said, this is a business, and many advisors will try to hook you by saying something extreme at the end of either the consultation or session. So beware of that as well and proceed with caution. There are ethical advisors, and you can tell who they are. They will not try to hook you and feed off of your fears, and you can tell when they are honest. They will tell you the good and the bad if necessary, and will even follow up with you on a human level instead of telling you they “received valuable information that you need to hear” and ask you to book a session. Again, it is a business, and even those who are legitimate may try to reel you in somehow, so take it with a grain of salt.

Like I said, the app has potential. PsychicBook just needs to do a better job at screening these advisors for legitimacy. I’d even understand inaccurate advisors, but advisors clearly using AI is simply too much - but hey, if people are falling for it and it’s bringing in money, why not, right?
